Entry Historiographical Limits of Yi Ti Most Western knowledge of the Yi lands comes from long-distance records written by sailors, merchants, scholars, and the Jade Sea Chronicles. They preserve precious legends, but also mix names, dates and foreign rituals; careful narratives should distinguish between "such legends of the Yidi people" Altars, relics, and prophecies can unite people and give a political claim the appearance of irrefutability.
